title: Orders per customer
prompt: Show each customer_id and how many orders it has, as orders. This reveals the one-to-many link. Replace the ___.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY id;
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders;

title: Items per order
prompt: Show each order_id and how many rows it has in order_items, as line_items.
hints: One row is one product in one order.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS line_items FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS line_items FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id;
SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS line_items FROM order_items GROUP BY product_id;

title: Many on the other side
prompt: A student can have many enrolments. Show the student_id of students with more than one enrolment.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (15, 8, 5, 50, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT student_id FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT student_id FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id;
SELECT id FROM enrolments GROUP BY id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
wrongSolutions.why: An id is unique, so this is empty

title: Sessions per user
prompt: Show each user_id and its number of sessions, as sessions.
solutions: SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS sessions FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS sessions FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date;
SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS sessions FROM sessions GROUP BY id;

title: What one row means
prompt: One order can have many rows in order_items. Show the row count as item_rows, and the number of different orders as orders.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT COUNT(*) AS item_rows, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders FROM order_items;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS item_rows, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM order_items;
wrongSolutions.why: Treats each row as an order

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) AS item_rows, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders FROM order_items;

title: Fix the grain
prompt: This should show how many times each product was sold, as times_sold, with one row per product_id. It runs but the grain is wrong. Fix it.
hints: Group by what each result row should represent.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS times_sold FROM order_items GROUP BY product_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS times_sold FROM order_items;
SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity) AS times_sold FROM order_items GROUP BY product_id;

title: Many-to-many
prompt: Students and courses connect through enrolments. Show each course_id and how many different students it has, as students.
hints: A student can retake a course, so use DISTINCT.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT course_id, COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) AS students FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS students FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id;
SELECT student_id, COUNT(DISTINCT course_id) AS students FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id;

title: Customer per month
prompt: Show each customer_id and month like 2024-01 as month, with their number of orders as orders. One result row is one customer in one month.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (14, 7, '2024-02-02', 'shipped');

solutions: SELECT customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id, month;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;
SELECT customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY month;
